surprised.description: an unexpected event, without assuming it is good or bad

annoyed.description: mild irritation, less intense than angry or furious

proud.description: satisfaction in one's own or another person's achievement

angry.description: clear anger at a wrong or obstacle, stronger than annoyed

grateful.description: appreciation for help, kindness, or a benefit received

lonely.description: distress from lacking companionship or connection

impressed.description: admiration caused by something notably skillful or good

afraid.description: fear of a concrete threat, less overwhelming than terrified

confident.description: belief in one's ability or a favorable outcome

hopeful.description: desire and belief that a positive outcome may happen

anxious.description: uneasy worry about an uncertain outcome

disappointed.description: sadness because an expectation was not met

joyful.description: strong happiness caused by a positive event

prepared.description: readiness because planning or practice is complete

guilty.description: remorse for one's own action or responsibility

nostalgic.description: longing for or warmly recalling the past

jealous.description: fear or resentment about losing status, attention, or a bond

anticipating.description: looking forward to an upcoming event; valence may be mixed

embarrassed.description: social discomfort after awkward exposure or attention

content.description: calm satisfaction, lower arousal than joyful or excited

devastated.description: overwhelming sadness after severe loss or bad news

sentimental.description: tender emotional attachment to a person, object, or memory

trusting.description: willingness to rely on another person or believe them

ashamed.description: painful negative judgment of oneself, broader than guilt about an act

apprehensive.description: cautious fear about a possible future problem

faithful.description: loyal commitment to a person, relationship, or belief

neutral.description: an explicitly expressed neutral state that is neither positive nor negative, such as feeling neither happy nor sad about something; distinct from contentment

no_emotion.description: the current input expresses no identifiable emotion, such as a purely factual question or task instruction; does not indicate recognition failure or uncertainty
